children.title: Active Constraint Geometry
children.top_down_role: Constraint activity associated with the current point and its containing face.

assumptions_latex: The feasible polyhedron is \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active constraints determine the minimal face of \(P\) containing \(x\) through their equality hyperplanes.

notation.meaning: Set of inequalities tight at a feasible point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral active-set geometry at a feasible QP iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in P\), define the active index set by \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i:(Gx)_i=h_i\}\). The face exposed by these tight inequalities is \(F(x)=\{y\in P:G_i y=h_i\ \text{for every }i\in\mathcal A(x)\}\). Its tangent space is \(T_{F(x)}=\{d:Ad=0,\ G_i d=0\ \text{for every }i\in\mathcal A(x)\}\), while feasible first-order directions additionally satisfy \(G_i d\le0\) for active inequalities that are not imposed as equalities by a chosen working face. Redundant active rows may describe the same face and need not be linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, tight inequalities define its active set, exposed face, tangent space, and cone of locally feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Constraint Geometry

children.title: Working Constraint Estimates
children.top_down_role: Algorithmic constraint subsets used to represent a candidate face.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaling Dependence of Absolute Slack Estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation dependence of a working-set estimate formed from unnormalized absolute slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality \(G_ix\le h_i\), replace its representation by \(\rho_iG_ix\le\rho_ih_i\), where \(\rho_i>0\). The feasible set and exact activity are unchanged, but the slack becomes \(\rho_i s_i(x)\). Hence membership in \(W_\tau(x)=\{i:s_i(x)\le\tau\}\) can change when \(\tau>0\). Invariance requires prescribed row normalization or row-specific thresholds transformed as \(\tau_i\mapsto\rho_i\tau_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive threshold applied to raw slacks depends on constraint scaling; normalization or correspondingly scaled thresholds are required for invariance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_\tau(x)\ \text{need not be invariant under }(G_i,h_i)\mapsto(\rho_iG_i,\rho_ih_i).

notation.meaning: positive scaling of inequality row i

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Dependence of Absolute Slack Estimates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-revealing removal of dependent estimated rows after consistency has been verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(C_Wy=d_W\) is consistent. Select indices \(J\) whose rows form a basis for the row space of \([C_W\ d_W]\). Then \[\{y:C_Wy=d_W\}=\{y:(C_W)_Jy=(d_W)_J\},\] and \((C_W)_J\) has full row rank. Thus a rank-revealing factorization of the augmented system may discard nonbasis rows without changing the estimated affine set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a consistent estimate, retaining an augmented-row basis removes dependence without changing the represented affine set.
assumptions_latex: J\text{ indexes a row basis of }[C_W\ d_W]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{sol}(C_W,d_W)=\operatorname{sol}((C_W)_J,(d_W)_J).

notation.meaning: indices of retained independent augmented rows

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Set-Preserving Rank Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for imposing estimated constraints as equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_Wy=d_W\) stack the original equalities and estimated working inequalities. Its affine solution set is nonempty exactly when \[d_W\in\operatorname{range}(C_W),\] equivalently \(u^Td_W=0\) for every \(u\in\ker(C_W^T)\), or \(C_WC_W^\dagger d_W=d_W\). Row dependence is harmless when these compatibility conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimated working equalities are consistent exactly when their right-hand sides satisfy every dependence among their normals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y:C_Wy=d_W\}\ne\varnothing\iff d_W\in\operatorname{range}(C_W).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the working-row matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Estimated-Face Consistency Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested, scale-invariant near-activity estimate for nonzero inequality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible \(x\) and rows \(G_i\ne0\), define \(\widehat s_i(x)=(h_i-G_ix)/\|G_i\|_2\) and \(\widehat W_\tau(x)=\{i:0\le\widehat s_i(x)\le\tau\}\). Then \(\widehat W_0(x)=\mathcal A(x)\), and \(\widehat W_{\tau_1}(x)\subseteq\widehat W_{\tau_2}(x)\) for \(0\le\tau_1\le\tau_2\). Positive row rescaling \((G_i,h_i)\mapsto(\rho_iG_i,\rho_ih_i)\) leaves both \(\widehat s_i\) and the estimate unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized slacks give nested working-constraint estimates that equal exact activity at zero tolerance and are invariant under positive row scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat W_0(x)=\mathcal A(x),\quad \tau_1\le\tau_2\Rightarrow\widehat W_{\tau_1}(x)\subseteq\widehat W_{\tau_2}(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Slack-Threshold Estimate

assumptions_latex: The current iterate satisfies \(x\in P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimate \(W_\tau(x)\) contains constraints whose current slack is at most \(\tau\), and equals the active set when \(\tau=0\).

notation.meaning: Slack vector for the inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A canonical slack-threshold estimate, not a claim that every implementation uses this rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the slack vector \(s(x)=h-Gx\ge0\). A canonical geometric estimate of the constraints defining the current or nearby face is \(W_\tau(x)=\{i:0\le s_i(x)\le\tau\}\). Hence \(W_0(x)=\mathcal A(x)\), and \(W_{\tau_1}(x)\subseteq W_{\tau_2}(x)\) whenever \(0\le\tau_1\le\tau_2\). The estimated working face is \(F_{W_\tau}(x)=\{y:Ay=b,\ G_i y=h_i\ \text{for every }i\in W_\tau(x)\}\). The estimate is admissible for an equality-constrained face solve only if this affine set is consistent; rank-revealing selection may remove dependent estimated rows without changing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraints with slack below a chosen tolerance form a nested estimate of the nearby active face; consistency and row dependence must be checked before a face solve.
knowledge_statements.title: Working Constraint Estimates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The slack-threshold construction is plausible and clearly labeled canonical, but working-set estimation and dependent-row handling require an inspectable active-set source.

children.title: Activity-Estimate Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Regimes where geometric activity differs from the maintained working-set estimate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that an underestimated working face can admit an infeasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1\ge0\}\), \(x=(0,0)\), and \(W=\varnothing\). The inequality is active but omitted. For \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1\), the working-face descent direction \(d=(-1,0)\) satisfies \(\nabla f(x)^Td=-1<0\), yet \(x+\alpha d\notin P\) for every \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting an active inequality can make the working-face model propose an immediately infeasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla f(x)^Td<0\quad\text{but}\quad x+\alpha d\notin P\ \text{for every }\alpha>0.

notation.meaning: descent direction admitted by the underestimated working face

knowledge_statements.title: Omitted-Active-Constraint Feasibility Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic certificate for equality of a working estimate and the pointwise active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E^+(W,x)=W\setminus\mathcal A(x)\), \(E^-(W,x)=\mathcal A(x)\setminus W\), and \(m(W,x)=|W\triangle\mathcal A(x)|\). Then \[W=\mathcal A(x)\iff E^+(W,x)=E^-(W,x)=\varnothing\iff m(W,x)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working estimate identifies the active set exactly if and only if both directed mismatches, equivalently their symmetric difference, vanish.
assumptions_latex: W\text{ and }\mathcal A(x)\text{ are finite index sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |W\triangle\mathcal A(x)|=0\iff W=\mathcal A(x).

notation.meaning: working indices that are inactive at x
active indices omitted from the working estimate

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Activity-Identification Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that an overestimated working set need not contain the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ge0\}\), take \(x=1\), and let \(W\) contain the sole inequality although it is inactive at \(x\). Imposing it as \(x=0\) gives the estimated face \(F_W=\{0\}\), so \(x\notin F_W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding an inactive constraint as an equality can produce a working-face estimate that excludes the current feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\notin F_W.

notation.meaning: affine set obtained by imposing working inequalities as equalities

knowledge_statements.title: Extra-Inactive-Constraint Face-Containment Failure

assumptions_latex: The true active set is \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i:(Gx)_i=h_i\}\), and \(W\) is a proposed working set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symmetric difference \(W\triangle\mathcal A(x)\) separates falsely retained constraints from omitted active constraints.

notation.meaning: Working constraints that are not active.
Active constraints omitted from the working set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic boundary between exact face identification and an erroneous working-set estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E^+(W,x)=W\setminus\mathcal A(x)\) and \(E^-(W,x)=\mathcal A(x)\setminus W\). Exact activity identification holds precisely when \(E^+(W,x)=E^-(W,x)=\varnothing\), equivalently \(W\triangle\mathcal A(x)=\varnothing\). An index in \(E^+(W,x)\) imposes an equality not satisfied by \(x\), so the purported working face need not contain the iterate. An index in \(E^-(W,x)\) removes a tight boundary equation from the face model, so a computed direction can point outside the feasible tangent cone. Therefore either nonempty mismatch set invalidates identification of the equality-constrained model with the actual active face, although a subsequent ratio test or constraint exchange may repair the estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working set is exact only when it has neither inactive extra constraints nor omitted active constraints; either mismatch invalidates its identification with the current face.
knowledge_statements.title: Activity-Estimate Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-theoretic mismatch definitions are coherent and the failure_boundary kind fits, but the algorithmic consequences of extra and omitted indices lack cited support.

children.title: Equality-Constrained Working-Face Models
children.top_down_role: Quadratic models restricted to the current estimated face.

assumptions_latex: The QP is \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), with \(Q=Q^T\).
The working set \(W\) is treated as equality constraints and \(K_W=[A^T\;G_W^T]^T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The working-face model is an equality-constrained QP whose stationary points satisfy the displayed saddle-point system.

notation.meaning: Combined matrix of permanent and working equalities.
Multipliers for permanent and working equalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained restriction of a linearly constrained quadratic program to a selected working face.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Newton-like Methods for Equality Constraints p. 234
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_W=[b^T\;h_W^T]^T\). Restricting the QP to the working face gives \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(K_Wx=r_W\). At a feasible face point \(x_k\), its step form is \(\min_p \tfrac12p^TQp+(Qx_k+c)^Tp\) subject to \(K_Wp=0\). A stationary pair \((p,y_W)\) satisfies \(\begin{bmatrix}Q&K_W^T\\K_W&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\y_W\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}Qx_k+c\\0\end{bmatrix}\). If \(K_W\) has full row rank and \(Q\) is positive definite on \(\ker K_W\), this system has a unique solution and the step is the unique face minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treating working inequalities as equalities yields an equality-constrained QP, represented by its face-tangent step problem and saddle-point KKT system.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Working-Face Models

children.title: Multiplier-Based Face Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual evidence used to retain or reject the current face.

The inequality convention is \(Gx\le h\), and stationarity is \(Qx+c+A^T\nu+G^T\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonnegative working multipliers together with primal feasibility and stationarity certify global optimality for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT sign certificate for retaining or rejecting inequalities on a convex-QP working face.

children.title: Primal-Feasible Initialization
children.top_down_role: Initialization regimes that begin from a feasible primal face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible feasible point and canonical initial working-set choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\) and \(I(x_0)=\{i:G_ix_0=h_i\}\). A primal-feasible active-set initialization is a pair \((x_0,W_0)\) satisfying \(x_0\in P\) and \(W_0\subseteq I(x_0)\). The maximal choice is \(W_0=I(x_0)\). If the working-face solver requires independent equations, dependent equality rows are first removed and \(W_0\) may be chosen so that \([A^T\ G_{W_0}^T]^T\) has full row rank. A basis choice that also spans the row space of \([A^T\ G_{I(x_0)}^T]^T\) has the same tangent null space as the maximal choice. Neither stationarity nor multiplier-sign feasibility is part of primal-feasible initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a feasible point and select only tight inequalities. One may use all tight constraints or an independent basis when the face solver requires it.
assumptions_latex: \text{Any rank requirement is imposed by the selected working-face solver.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_0\in P,\quad W_0\subseteq I(x_0);\qquad \operatorname{row}(A,G_{W_0})=\operatorname{row}(A,G_{I(x_0)})\Rightarrow\ker(A,G_{W_0})=\ker(A,G_{I(x_0)}).

notation.meaning: Tight inequality indices at the initial point.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasible Active-Set Initialization

assumptions_latex: The constraint set is \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid primal-feasible initialization is a pair \((x_0,W_0)\) with \(x_0\in P\) and \(W_0\subseteq\mathcal A(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization condition for active-set iterations that must preserve primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-feasible initialization consists of \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and a working set \(W_0\) satisfying \(Ax_0=b\), \(Gx_0\le h\), and \(W_0\subseteq\mathcal A(x_0)=\{i:G_ix_0=h_i\}\). If the initial face model requires independent normals, the rows of \([A^T\;G_{W_0}^T]^T\) must additionally have full row rank after redundant rows are removed. This condition supplies a feasible initial face for methods whose line search truncates steps at newly encountered constraints. It does not impose stationarity or dual feasibility; those are established through face minimization and working-set exchanges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-feasible initialization requires a feasible point and a working set drawn from its tight constraints, with dependent rows removed when the face solver requires full rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasible Initialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The initialization condition is standard and internally consistent, but no inspectable source supports the active-set-specific rank and initialization requirements.

children.top_down_role: Initialization regimes that begin from a dual-feasible estimate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stationarity and sign-feasibility condition, including the singular-Hessian range boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Q\succeq0\) and \(L(x,
u,\lambda)=	frac12x^TQx+c^Tx+
u^T(Ax-b)+\lambda^T(Gx-h)\), a stationary dual-feasible start is a triple \((x_0,
u_0,\lambda_0)\) satisfying \[Qx_0+c+A^T
u_0+G^T\lambda_0=0,\qquad \lambda_0\ge0.\] Equivalently, a multiplier pair \((
u_0,\lambda_0)\) admits such an \(x_0\) exactly when \(\lambda_0\ge0\) and \(c+A^T
u_0+G^T\lambda_0\in\operatorname{Range}(Q)\), in which case \[x_0=-Q^\dagger(c+A^T
u_0+G^T\lambda_0)+z,\qquad z\in\ker Q.\] When \(Q\succ0\), this reduces to the unique formula with \(Q^{-1}\). Primal feasibility and complementarity are not required by this initialization condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible start enforces stationarity and nonnegative inequality multipliers. With a singular Hessian it exists only under a range condition; with a positive-definite Hessian it is unique for fixed multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x_0:\ Qx_0+c+A^T\nu_0+G^T\lambda_0=0\iff \lambda_0\ge0\ \text{and}\ c+A^T\nu_0+G^T\lambda_0\in\operatorname{Range}(Q).

assumptions_latex: The QP uses inequalities \(Gx\le h\) and Lagrangian stationarity \(Qx+c+A^T\nu+G^T\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dual-feasible initialization satisfies stationarity and \(\lambda_0\ge0\), although \(x_0\) may violate primal inequalities.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dual-feasible starting triple \((x_0,\nu_0,\lambda_0)\) satisfies \(Qx_0+c+A^T\nu_0+G^T\lambda_0=0\) and \(\lambda_0\ge0\). Equality feasibility \(Ax_0=b\), inequality feasibility \(Gx_0\le h\), and complementarity \(\lambda_{0i}(G_ix_0-h_i)=0\) are not required by dual feasibility alone. A compatible initial working estimate may be defined by \(W_0=\{i:\lambda_{0i}>0\}\), optionally augmented by zero-multiplier indices. Dual active-set iterations then preserve the multiplier sign condition while exchanging constraints to reduce primal infeasibility and ultimately seek the remaining KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible start satisfies stationarity with nonnegative inequality multipliers, while primal feasibility and complementarity may initially fail and are repaired by constraint exchanges.

children.title: Active-Set Phase-I Methods
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary face-navigation families for finding primal feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Always-feasible auxiliary LP for mixed equality and inequality feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), solve \[\Phi^*=\min_{x,p,n,v}\ \mathbf1^T(p+n)+\mathbf1^Tv\] subject to \[Ax-b=p-n,\qquad Gx-h\le v,\qquad p,n,v\ge0.\] The auxiliary LP is feasible for all finite data and has an attained finite optimum. Moreover, \(\Phi^*=0\) if and only if \(P\ne\varnothing\). A zero optimum returns a feasible \(x^*\); a positive optimum, together with an optimal auxiliary dual solution, provides a checkable infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize total equality artificials and inequality violations. The optimum is zero exactly when the original constraints are feasible.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is unrestricted, and }p,n,v\text{ are componentwise nonnegative.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi^*=0\iff\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Fully Elastic Linear Phase I

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-termination and worst-case boundary for simplex-style active-set solution of the auxiliary LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simplex-style Phase-I implementation using an anti-cycling pivot rule terminates after finitely many bases and returns the auxiliary optimum or its dual certificate. Without an anti-cycling rule, degeneracy can cause repeated bases; finite termination does not imply a polynomial pivot bound, since exponentially long pivot paths are possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anti-cycling gives finite Phase-I pivot termination, but degeneracy can otherwise cycle and finite termination is not a polynomial-time guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary LP is solved by exact simplex-style basis pivots.
A finite anti-cycling rule is used for the finite-termination conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{anti-cycling}\Rightarrow\text{finite basis termination},\qquad \text{finite termination}\not\Rightarrow\text{polynomial pivot complexity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-I Pivot Termination Boundary

assumptions_latex: The linear constraint system is \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\).
The auxiliary problem is solved to global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Phase-I optimum \(t^*=0\) yields a feasible point for the original constraints; \(t^*>0\) certifies infeasibility of this system.
review_flags: specific authoritative active-set Phase-I locator unavailable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-slack linear Phase-I construction for finding feasibility before QP optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \((A,b,G,h)\). Initialize any \(x^{(0)}\) satisfying \(Ax^{(0)}=b\), when the equalities are consistent, and set \(t^{(0)}=\max\{0,\max_i(G_ix^{(0)}-h_i)\}\). Solve the auxiliary linear program \(\min_{x,t}t\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(Gx-h\le t\mathbf1\), and \(t\ge0\), using working-face steps and ratio tests. Stop at a global minimizer \((x^*,t^*)\). If \(t^*=0\), output \(x^*\), which is feasible for the original constraints, together with its tight-constraint working set. If \(t^*>0\), report that the original linear constraint system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a common nonnegative constraint-violation variable by active-set steps; zero optimum provides a feasible start, while a positive global optimum proves the constraints infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Phase-I Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Phase-I conclusion is valid only when the equality system is consistent and the auxiliary LP has an optimum. As written, the algorithm does not handle inconsistent equalities despite claiming to diagnose the full constraint system, and it has no source.

Projection-Induced Identification Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of stable active-face identification without strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(q_\varepsilon(x)=\tfrac12x^2-\varepsilon x\) on \(\Omega=[0,\infty)\). Its unique solution is \(x_\varepsilon^*=\max\{\varepsilon,0\}\). For \(\varepsilon<0\), the lower bound is active with multiplier \(-\varepsilon>0\); for \(\varepsilon>0\), the solution is interior; and at \(\varepsilon=0\), the solution lies on the bound with zero multiplier. Thus arbitrarily small perturbations of the gradient change the correct active face at the degenerate instance. Projection alone cannot provide locally stable finite identification there; strict complementarity or an equivalent separation condition is needed for robust face identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a zero-multiplier active bound, arbitrarily small objective perturbations switch the solution between boundary and interior, so projection cannot stably identify the face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\varepsilon=0\), active-face identification is not locally invariant under perturbations of \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If R=Z^THZ\succ0, conjugate gradients applied to Rp=-g reaches the exact reduced minimizer in at most \dim\ker B iterations in exact arithmetic. If the eigenvalues of R lie in [m,L], then \|p_k-p^*\|_R\le2((\sqrt{L/m}-1)/(\sqrt{L/m}+1))^k\|p_0-p^*\|_R.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness for the unrestricted reduced subspace problem, before face-bound truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R=Z^THZ and g=Z^T(Hx_F+c). If R\succ0, the affine-hull restriction has the unique minimizer p^*=-R^{-1}g. If R\succeq0, it has a minimizer exactly when g\in\operatorname{range}(R), in which case the minimizers solve Rp=-g. If g\notin\operatorname{range}(R), the affine-hull quadratic is unbounded below along a null direction. Then x=x_F+Zp and q(x)=\tfrac12p^T(Z^THZ)p+[Z^T(Hx_F+c)]^Tp+q(x_F). The reduced stationarity equation is (Z^THZ)p=-Z^T(Hx_F+c).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact free-coordinate Newton step with first-bound refinement on a box face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x lie on a box face with fixed coordinates \mathcal A and free coordinates \mathcal F. Solve H_{\mathcal F\mathcal F}p_{\mathcal F}=-\nabla_{\mathcal F}q(x) and set p_{\mathcal A}=0. Define \beta_*=\min\left\{1,\min_{i\in\mathcal F:p_i<0}(x_i-\ell_i)/(-p_i),\min_{i\in\mathcal F:p_i>0}(u_i-x_i)/p_i\right\}, with an empty inner minimum equal to +\infty, and set x^+=x+\beta_*p. If \beta_*=1, x^+ is the affine-hull minimizer and has zero free gradient. If \beta_*<1, every index attaining the minimum reaches a bound and is fixed there in the refined face; all simultaneous hitters are added together.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take the exact free Newton direction, truncate it at the first bound, and either finish the affine-hull minimization or refine the face with every hitting coordinate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a box face with active coordinates \(\mathcal A\) fixed at \(\bar x_{\mathcal A}\) and free coordinates \(\mathcal F\). For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\), solve \(H_{\mathcal F\mathcal F}p_{\mathcal F}=-\nabla_{\mathcal F}q(x)\) and set \(p_{\mathcal A}=0\). Choose the largest \(\beta\in[0,1]\) for which \(x+\beta p\) remains in the face bounds, and update \(x^+=x+\beta p\). If \(\beta=1\), the free-gradient vanishes at \(x^+\); otherwise, at least one free coordinate reaches a boundary and the candidate face is refined.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a fixed-face KKT matrix is singular, that active set need not determine a unique affine primal-dual candidate. Semidefinite curvature can permit multiple primal optimizers, while dependent active rows can permit multiple multipliers even with a unique primal optimizer. Convexity alone therefore does not guarantee a unique continuous piecewise-affine primal-dual selection.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the Critical Parameter Regions assumptions, suppose additionally that H is constant, c(\theta) is affine, and the objective constant term is at most quadratic in \theta. If x^*(\theta)=X\theta+x_0 on a critical region, then substituting x^*(\theta) into the objective gives a quadratic function v(\theta) on that region. The value is continuous across adjacent regions whenever the unique primal optimizer is continuous.

The objective's parameter-only term has degree at most two.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a strongly convex QP with constant H and A and with c(\theta) and b(\theta) affine in \theta. For a fixed active set \mathcal A whose KKT matrix is nonsingular, the primal-dual candidate (x_{\mathcal A}(\theta),\lambda_{\mathcal A}(\theta)) is affine in \theta. Its validity region is \mathcal R_{\mathcal A}=\{\theta:r_{\mathcal I}(\theta)\ge0,\ \lambda_{\mathcal A}(\theta)\ge0\}, hence is polyhedral.

The fixed-active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular.

assumptions_latex: \Theta is a polyhedron on which the feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*:\Theta\to\mathbb R^n\ \text{is unique, continuous, and affine on every cell of a finite polyhedral subdivision}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global primal structure for a fixed-matrix strongly convex affine-parametric QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H\succ0 and A be fixed, and let c(\theta) and b(\theta) be affine in \theta. On a polyhedral parameter domain \Theta for which \{x:Ax\ge b(\theta)\} is nonempty, the QP has a unique optimizer x^*(\theta). The domain admits a finite polyhedral subdivision such that x^* is affine on each cell and continuous on \Theta. Multipliers are affine on each regular fixed-active-set cell, but dependent active rows may make them nonunique; consequently an arbitrary cellwise multiplier choice need not define a continuous global selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly convex fixed-matrix multiparametric QP has a continuous piecewise-affine primal optimizer, while degeneracy may make its multipliers nonunique or prevent arbitrary cellwise choices from matching continuously.

Parametric QP Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise-affine solution tracking for a strongly convex affine-parametric QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x\tfrac12x^THx+(c_0+tc_1)^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b_0+tb_1\), where \(t\) ranges over an interval. On any subinterval with fixed active set \(\mathcal A\) satisfying LICQ, the primal-dual solution obeys \[\begin{pmatrix}H&-A_{\mathcal A}^T\\A_{\mathcal A}&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x(t)\\\lambda_{\mathcal A}(t)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-(c_0+tc_1)\\b_{0,\mathcal A}+tb_{1,\mathcal A}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \lambda_{\mathcal I}(t)=0.\] Hence \((x(t),\lambda_{\mathcal A}(t))\) is affine in \(t\) until an inactive slack or active multiplier reaches zero, producing a breakpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed regular active set, the parametric QP solution is affine in the parameter; breakpoints occur when a slack or multiplier reaches zero.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is nonempty throughout the parameter interval.
Active constraint rows are linearly independent on each tracked segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution path is continuous and piecewise affine, with changes confined to complementarity breakpoints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional event-driven tracking for a scalar affine-data convex QP homotopy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from a KKT point z_k at t_k with a compatible partition \mathcal A_k. Solve the derivative equations of the nonsingular fixed-face KKT system and advance in the prescribed direction to the target or the first positive complementarity event, whichever comes first. At an event collect every zero-margin index in E. In a fixed deterministic order, test partitions obtained by changing only indices in E; for each candidate, solve its KKT system and recompute the one-sided derivatives of its inactive slacks and active multipliers. Accept the first nonsingular candidate having the required one-sided signs. If another margin is zero at the same parameter, perform a zero-length pivot and repeat. Reject any repeated pair (t_k,\mathcal A), and report a degeneracy failure if no admissible unvisited candidate exists. Otherwise continue to the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track each regular affine KKT segment to its first event, resolve tied and zero-length pivots deterministically, validate the new partition on the outgoing side, and stop at the target or an unresolved degeneracy.

assumptions_latex: The initial point is a KKT point of the initial convex QP.
Every accepted segment satisfies the parameterized KKT equations and complementarity.
The target is reached after finitely many regular segments and zero-length pivots.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a regular event-driven homotopy starts from a correct KKT point, every accepted segment and event update preserves the KKT equations and complementarity, and finitely many accepted transitions reach t=1, then the returned endpoint is a KKT point of \mathcal Q(1). If no active partition is revisited, at most 2^m partitions can be accepted. This bound is exponential; without finite arrival, nonrevisiting, and regularity, cycling, branching, or premature failure remains possible.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a KKT solution at \(t_k\) and its active set \(\mathcal A_k\), differentiate the fixed-active-set KKT equations to obtain \((\dot x,\dot\lambda_{\mathcal A_k})\). For each inactive constraint compute the first positive \(\Delta t\) at which its affine slack becomes zero; for each active constraint compute the first positive \(\Delta t\) at which its affine multiplier becomes zero. Take the smallest admissible event time, set \(t_{k+1}=t_k+\Delta t\), and update \((x,\lambda)\) affinely. Admit all blocking indices or release all zero-multiplier indices selected by a fixed tie rule. Repeat until the target parameter is reached.

assumptions_latex: The parametric QP satisfies the hypotheses of piecewise-affine tracking.
Each post-event active set yields a nonsingular reduced KKT matrix.
A deterministic rule resolves simultaneous events.

children.title: Face-Transition Events
children.top_down_role: Breakpoint structure associated with changes in the tracked active face.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of interpreting zero complementarity margins as a unique adjacent-face update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Simultaneous vanishing of several inactive slacks or active multipliers, weak activity r_i=\lambda_i=0, and redundant active rows can leave more than one admissible post-event active subset, with distinct subsets possibly representing the same geometric face. Complementarity alone therefore does not select a unique update; a tie rule and a solvability or regularity check for the post-event KKT system are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple zeros, weak activity, and redundant constraints can make the post-event active set nonunique.
assumptions_latex: Transitions are represented by nonnegative primal slacks and multipliers satisfying complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{zero complementarity margin}\not\Rightarrow\text{a unique post-event active subset}.

notation.meaning: A weakly active constraint with neither a primal nor dual margin.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Face-Event Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict-Margin Persistence of a Tracked Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local absence of complementarity events on a continuous tracked branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r_{\mathcal I}(t) and \lambda_{\mathcal A}(t) be continuous at t_0. If r_i(t_0)>0 for every i\in\mathcal I and \lambda_j(t_0)>0 for every j\in\mathcal A, then there is \varepsilon>0 such that these inequalities remain strict whenever |t-t_0|<\varepsilon; hence no slack- or multiplier-zero event occurs there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive inactive slacks and active multipliers exclude a nearby face-transition event.
assumptions_latex: The tracked slacks and multipliers are continuous at t_0.
Indices in \mathcal A and \mathcal I retain their complementarity roles until an event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\varepsilon>0:\ |t-t_0|<\varepsilon\Rightarrow r_{\mathcal I}(t)>0,\ \lambda_{\mathcal A}(t)>0.

notation.meaning: Tracked active and inactive index sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Margin Persistence of a Tracked Face

assumptions_latex: The tracked slacks and active multipliers are affine in the forward parameter s\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_*=\sup\{s\ge0:r_{\mathcal I}(u)\ge0,\ \lambda_{\mathcal A}(u)\ge0\ \forall u\in[0,s]\}.

notation.meaning: Current active and inactive index sets.
First forward complementarity-margin event, possibly positive infinity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-event formula on a regular affine complementarity segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r_i(s)=r_i^0+s\dot r_i for i\in\mathcal I and \lambda_j(s)=\lambda_j^0+s\dot\lambda_j for j\in\mathcal A, with r_i^0>0 and \lambda_j^0>0. Define s_*=\min\left(\{-r_i^0/\dot r_i:i\in\mathcal I,\ \dot r_i<0\}\cup\{-\lambda_j^0/\dot\lambda_j:j\in\mathcal A,\ \dot\lambda_j<0\}\right), where \min\varnothing=+\infty. Then r_{\mathcal I}(s)>0 and \lambda_{\mathcal A}(s)>0 for 0\le s<s_*. If s_*<+\infty, exactly the indices attaining the minimum have zero margin at s_*; multiple minimizers form a simultaneous event. If s_*=+\infty, no finite forward event occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first face event is the least zero time among slacks and multipliers moving toward zero; an empty candidate set means that no finite forward event occurs.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional First Face-Event Distance
Face-Transition Events
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementarity events delimiting fixed-face segments of a parametric QP path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a fixed-active-set segment parameterized by \(s\ge0\), write inactive slacks as \(r_i(s)=r_i^0+s\dot r_i\) and active multipliers as \(\lambda_j(s)=\lambda_j^0+s\dot\lambda_j\). A face-transition event occurs at the smallest \(s_*>0\) satisfying either \(r_i(s_*)=0\) for some inactive \(i\), which admits a blocking constraint, or \(\lambda_j(s_*)=0\) for some active \(j\), which permits release. Validity of the current face requires \(r_i(s)\ge0\) and \(\lambda_j(s)\ge0\) for \(0\le s\le s_*\). Simultaneous equalities define a multiple event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tracked face changes at the first zero of an inactive slack or active multiplier; ties constitute a multiple transition event.
assumptions_latex: Slacks and active multipliers are affine on the current segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_*\) is the maximal forward distance for which the current complementarity partition remains valid.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the face-transition leaf. The first-zero description is correct only after restricting attention to quantities moving toward zero and assuming strictly positive slack and multiplier values at the start of the open segment; it also omits the no-finite-event case. Without those qualifications, the claimed maximal forward distance is not fully defined. A parametric active-set source is required to fix the precise event conditions.

children.title: Working-Set Transition Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Mechanism families for moving among neighboring feasible faces.

children.title: Blocking-Constraint Admission
children.top_down_role: Face transitions caused by newly encountered boundaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximal feasible step, tied blockers, and the corresponding admission certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) satisfy \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\), and let \(p\) preserve all current working equalities. Define \(I^- =\{i\notin W:a_i^Tp<0\}\), \(\alpha_i=(a_i^Tx-b_i)/(-a_i^Tp)\), and \(\bar\alpha=\min\{1,\min_{i\in I^-}\alpha_i\}\), with the inner minimum interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(I^-=\varnothing\). Set \(x^+=x+\bar\alpha p\). If \(\bar\alpha<1\), the tied-blocker set \(B=\{i\in I^-:\alpha_i=\bar\alpha\}\) is nonempty; admit one member under a single-admission rule or any prescribed nonempty subset under a multiple-admission rule. The point \(x^+\) is feasible and every member of \(B\) is tight there. If \(\bar\alpha=1\), the full trial step is feasible and no blocking admission is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take the minimum blocking ratio, preserve feasibility, and admit one or more constraints tied at the first encountered boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax^+\ge b,\qquad a_i^Tx^+=b_i\ \forall i\in B.

notation.meaning: nonworking inequalities approached by the direction
constraints tied at the first blocking step
maximal feasible step capped at the full trial step

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking Ratio and Admission Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary cases in the blocking ratio test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inequality \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\) not currently in the working set, if \(a_i^Tp\ge0\), motion along \(p\) cannot violate it and it is excluded from the blocking minimum. If \(a_i^Tp<0\) and \(a_i^Tx=b_i\), its blocking ratio is zero; every positive step is infeasible, so it must be admitted, the direction changed, or a degenerate transition handled before positive progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only approached inequalities can block; an approached zero-slack constraint blocks at step zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_i^Tp\ge0\Rightarrow i\text{ does not block};\quad a_i^Tp<0,\ a_i^Tx=b_i\Rightarrow\alpha_i=0.
review_flags: clarified_inactive: the index is outside the working set but may already be geometrically active
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Distance and Nonapproached Constraints
Blocking-Constraint Admission
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible active-set step truncated by the first newly active inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) satisfy \(Ax\ge b\), let \(p\) be a search direction satisfying the current working-set equalities, and suppose the full trial step is \(x+p\). For every inactive index with \(a_i^Tp<0\), compute \(\alpha_i=(a_i^Tx-b_i)/(-a_i^Tp)\). Set \(\alpha=\min\{1,\min_i\alpha_i\}\) and update \(x^+=x+\alpha p\). If \(\alpha<1\), admit an index attaining the minimum into the working set, or admit all minimizers under a multiple-admission rule. If \(\alpha=1\), retain the working set. The update preserves primal feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shorten a feasible search step at the earliest inactive boundary and add the blocking constraint or tied blockers to the working set.
assumptions_latex: The direction preserves all current working-set equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax^+\ge b\), and every admitted blocker satisfies \(a_i^Tx^+=b_i\).

notation.meaning: Step length to inactive constraint i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits blocking-constraint admission, and the ratio test preserves feasibility under the stated inequality convention. No authoritative source is supplied. A standard feasible active-set QP reference with a specific algorithm, section, or page locator is required.

children.title: Multiplier-Driven Constraint Release
children.top_down_role: Face transitions prompted by incompatible multiplier status.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of indexwise negative-multiplier release when working-set multipliers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda_W=\{\lambda:A_W^{\mathsf T}\lambda=Hx+c\}\). If \(A_W\) has dependent rows, \(\Lambda_W\) may contain both a vector with a negative component and a nonnegative vector. For duplicate rows with \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\), both \((2,-1)\in\Lambda_W\) and \((1,0)\in\Lambda_W\). Thus a negative component of an arbitrary computed multiplier does not prove that the represented face lacks a dual-feasible multiplier; the invariant test is whether \(\Lambda_W\cap\mathbb R_+^{|W|}\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With dependent working rows, multiplier signs depend on the chosen representation, so an arbitrary negative component is not by itself a valid release certificate.
assumptions_latex: Working-set rows may be linearly dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Lambda_W\cap\mathbb R_+^{|W|}\ne\varnothing\) is the invariant dual-feasibility condition.

notation.meaning: affine set of working-set multipliers satisfying stationarity

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Nonuniqueness Release Boundary
Multiplier-Driven Constraint Release
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Working-set release triggered by violation of dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible point \(x\), suppose the equality-constrained QP over working set \(\mathcal W\) has zero primal search direction. Compute multipliers from \(Hx+c-A_{\mathcal W}^T\lambda_{\mathcal W}=0\), with \(\lambda_i=0\) outside \(\mathcal W\). If every \(\lambda_i\ge0\), stop: the convex QP KKT conditions hold. Otherwise choose an index \(j\in\arg\min_{i\in\mathcal W}\lambda_i\), remove \(j\) from \(\mathcal W\), and resolve the equality-constrained subproblem. A deterministic tie rule or anti-cycling rule selects among equal negative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the face minimizer has a negative active multiplier, release such a constraint and resolve; nonnegative multipliers certify optimality.
assumptions_latex: The inequality convention is \(Ax\ge b\) with nonnegative optimal multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either the current feasible point satisfies the QP KKT conditions, or a dual-infeasible active constraint is removed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits multiplier-driven release, and nonnegative working-set multipliers at a feasible face minimizer give the convex-QP KKT conditions. The assumption that working-set rows merely permit multiplier computation is too vague to determine uniqueness and selection under dependence or degeneracy. An authoritative active-set QP source with explicit multiplier and release conditions is required.

children.title: Constraint-Exchange Granularity Classes
children.top_down_role: Scalar and block modifications of the current working set.

children.title: Single-Constraint Exchange
children.top_down_role: Working-set transitions involving one admitted or released constraint.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic validity tests for adding or deleting exactly one working constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_W\) have full row rank. Adding row \(c_j^T\) preserves full row rank exactly when \(c_j^T\notin\operatorname{row}(C_W)\). Deleting any one row from \(C_W\) leaves the remaining rows independent. Thus scalar admission requires an independence test or redundant-row policy, whereas scalar release is rank-safe when the current working rows are independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-row admission must add an independent normal; deleting one row from an independent working system cannot create dependence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}[C_W;c_j^T]=\operatorname{rank}(C_W)+1\iff c_j^T\notin\operatorname{row}(C_W).
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Valid Scalar Admission and Release

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition-count convention separating actual exchanges from primal steps that leave the set unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scalar working-set transition is an event from \(W\) to \(W^+\) satisfying \(|W^+\triangle W|=1\). Equivalently, exactly one index is admitted or exactly one index is released. A primal step with \(W^+=W\) is an iteration event but not a working-set transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single exchange constrains actual working-set changes; an unchanged full primal step is not an exchange.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{scalar transition}\iff |W^+\triangle W|=1;\qquad W^+=W\Rightarrow\text{no transition}.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Working-Set Transition
Single-Constraint Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Working-set transition changing exactly one constraint per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a working set \(\mathcal W^k\), solve its equality-constrained QP subproblem. If the resulting direction is nonzero, take the maximal feasible step; when blocked, choose exactly one blocking index \(j\) by a deterministic tie rule and set \(\mathcal W^{k+1}=\mathcal W^k\cup\{j\}\). If the direction is zero and some working-set multiplier is negative, choose exactly one such index \(j\) and set \(\mathcal W^{k+1}=\mathcal W^k\setminus\{j\}\). Otherwise terminate. Thus every nonterminal transition satisfies \(|\mathcal W^{k+1}\triangle\mathcal W^k|=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration adds one blocker or removes one dual-infeasible constraint, so consecutive working sets differ in exactly one index.
assumptions_latex: The current primal iterate is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every nonterminal iteration, \(|\mathcal W^{k+1}\triangle\mathcal W^k|=1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the exchange-granularity leaf, but the universal conclusion about every nonterminal transition is not fully justified as written: a nonzero direction can take an unblocked full step while leaving the working set unchanged before the next optimality test. The record must define iteration boundaries so that such a step is not counted as a working-set transition. A source for the single-exchange convention and any degeneracy or anti-cycling requirements is also needed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deterministic Tie-Breaking Does Not Prevent Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on convergence claims based solely on deterministic scalar selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic tie rule makes the selected index a function of the current algorithmic state, but it does not imply that states cannot recur. Deterministic selection alone therefore supplies neither a strictly decreasing merit quantity nor finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choosing tied indices deterministically is not, by itself, an anti-cycling proof.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{determinism alone}\not\Rightarrow\text{finite termination}.
review_flags: disposition_defer: anti-cycling consequences are primarily owned by Degenerate Transition Handling or Exchange-Granularity Tradeoffs, not the scalar-granularity definition leaf
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Tie-Breaking Does Not Prevent Cycling

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf completely owns the definition and immediate rank validity of actual one-index working-set transitions, including the distinction between an exchange and an unchanged primal step. Blocker selection belongs to Blocking-Constraint Admission; multiplier selection belongs to Multiplier-Driven Constraint Release; multi-index changes belong to Multiple-Constraint Exchange; cycling safeguards and comparative progress belong to Degenerate Transition Handling and Exchange-Granularity Tradeoffs.

children.title: Multiple-Constraint Exchange
children.top_down_role: Block transitions involving several simultaneous working-set modifications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank test for adding a block of newly tight inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_W\) have full row rank and let \(C_B\) contain candidate blocker rows. Simultaneous admission preserves full row rank exactly when \[\operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}C_W\\C_B\end{bmatrix}=\operatorname{rank}(C_W)+|B|.\] Equivalently, the restrictions of the new row functionals to \(\ker C_W\) are linearly independent. If the condition fails, a maximal independent subset may represent the same reached affine face while the remaining tight rows are recorded as algebraically redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blocker batch is rank-safe exactly when its new normals are independent modulo the existing working rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The augmented rows have full row rank iff their rank increases by }|B|.

notation.meaning: current equality and working-constraint row matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Preserving Simultaneous Admission Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that admitting every tied blocker can make the working-row system dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R\), represent the boundary by \(x\ge0\) and \(2x\ge0\). From \(x=1\) with \(p=-1\), both constraints block at \(\alpha=1\). Admitting both gives working rows \([1;2]\), which are dependent, although either row alone represents the reached face \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tied blockers can be redundant, so admitting all of them may create a singular working-row system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}[1;2]=1<2.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependent Tied-Blocker Batch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Granularity definition independent of the mechanism selecting admissions or releases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiple-constraint exchange is an actual working-set transition from \(W\) to \(W^+\) satisfying \(|W^+\triangle W|\ge2\). Writing \(B=W^+\setminus W\) and \(R=W\setminus W^+\), one has \(W^+=(W\cup B)\setminus R\), \(B\cap R=\varnothing\), and \(|B|+|R|\ge2\). A primal step with \(W^+=W\) is not an exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiple exchange is a working-set change involving at least two admitted or released indices; unchanged primal steps are not exchanges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{multiple exchange}\iff |W^+\triangle W|\ge2.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Working-Set Transition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Validity of Block Admission and Release
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local feasibility effect of simultaneous working-set changes at a feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible iterate \(x\), every admitted inequality must be tight at \(x\); adding any collection of such equalities preserves containment of \(x\) in the new working affine set. Releasing any collection of working equalities also preserves primal feasibility of \(x\). These facts do not guarantee row independence or progress of the subsequent face solve, which require separate tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding constraints already tight at the iterate or releasing working constraints preserves feasibility of the current point, but not necessarily rank or progress.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ remains feasible and satisfies every equality retained or admitted in }W^+.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Validity of Block Admission and Release
Multiple-Constraint Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batched admission or release at a working-set transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a working set \(\mathcal W^k\), compute a feasible working-set step and its multipliers. At a blocking step, let \(B\) be a nonempty selected subset of inactive constraints attaining the minimum feasible step length and set \(\mathcal W^{k+1}=\mathcal W^k\cup B\). At a face minimizer with dual infeasibility, let \(R\) be a nonempty selected subset of active indices having negative multipliers and set \(\mathcal W^{k+1}=\mathcal W^k\setminus R\). Before resolving, remove dependent additions or regularize the reduced KKT system according to a prescribed rank policy. Terminate only when no admission or release condition applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch tied blockers or several negative-multiplier constraints into one transition, while enforcing a rank policy before solving the next reduced system.
assumptions_latex: The current primal iterate is feasible.
Batch selection preserves a solvable or explicitly regularized reduced KKT system.
Admissions and releases are selected by fixed rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonterminal update has \(\mathcal W^{k+1}=(\mathcal W^k\cup B)\setminus R\) with \(|B|+|R|\ge1\), potentially exceeding one.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits multiple-constraint exchange, but batching several negative-multiplier releases and repairing rank by an unspecified policy are method-dependent operations requiring a concrete source. The body describes admission and release as alternative transitions, whereas the conclusion uses both B and R without defining the unused set as empty; this must be made consistent. A cited batched active-set method must determine the admissible batch and rank-handling rules.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial bound based only on distinct working-set enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(m\) inequalities, if every nonterminal exchange changes the working set and no working set is revisited, at most \(2^m-1\) nonterminal exchanges occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonrevisiting exchange process visits at most the finite collection of working sets, although that collection is exponential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \#\{\text{nonterminal exchanges}\}\le2^m-1.
review_flags: disposition_defer: duplicates the ancestor-level Active-Set Worst-Case Complexity Boundary and is not specific to multiple exchange
knowledge_statements.title: Nonrevisiting Block-Exchange Termination Bound

Blocker selection belongs to Blocking-Constraint Admission; multiplier selection belongs to Multiplier-Driven Constraint Release; scalar changes belong to Single-Constraint Exchange; progress and factorization tradeoffs belong to Exchange-Granularity Tradeoffs.

children.title: Exchange-Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Stability, progress, and factorization implications of scalar versus block exchanges.

knowledge_statements.title: Exchange-Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares single- and multiple-constraint working-set exchanges for feasible active-set QP iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^T Hx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), and let \(W_k\) be the working set. A single exchange restricts \(|W_{k+1}\triangle W_k|=1\); a multiple exchange permits a larger symmetric difference. Single exchanges require fewer constraint-status decisions per iteration and permit deterministic pivot-level tie breaking, but may need several iterations to realize one face transition. Multiple exchanges can realize that transition at once, but the updated constraint gradients must remain consistent and the resulting equality-constrained subproblem must be well posed. Thus exchange granularity trades iteration count against transition validation and degeneracy handling; neither rule uniformly dominates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single exchanges simplify validation and tie-breaking but may require more iterations; multiple exchanges move between faces faster but require stronger consistency and degeneracy checks.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\succeq0\) and the feasible set is nonempty.
Each accepted working set defines a solvable equality-constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{larger exchange granularity}\Longleftrightarrow\text{fewer potential transitions but more validation per transition}\).

notation.meaning: working-set index set at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and container fit, but the comparative claims depend on a specific active-set algorithm. Larger exchanges do not inherently guarantee fewer transitions, and no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Degenerate Transition Handling
children.top_down_role: Transition mechanisms for coincident boundaries and weakly active constraints.

children.title: Degenerate-Pivot Handling
children.top_down_role: Transition safeguards for ambiguous pivots caused by weak or coincident activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Pivot Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic pivot rule for working-set changes that produce no primal progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible iterate \(x_k\), working set \(W_k\), search direction \(p_k\), and blocking ratios, form the tied blocker set \(B_k\) of constraints attaining the minimum nonnegative ratio. If the minimum ratio is zero, select the entering constraint by a fixed lexicographic order. If the equality-constrained stationarity test instead exposes nonpositive multipliers, select the leaving constraint lexicographically among the minimum admissible multipliers. Update \(W_k\) without requiring \(x_k\) to change, refactor the working-set system, and repeat. Stop with \(x_k\) only when primal feasibility, stationarity, and multiplier sign conditions all hold; otherwise output the first subsequently accepted positive step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a degenerate pivot, change one tied constraint by a fixed lexicographic rule, refactor, and continue until optimality or a positive step occurs.
assumptions_latex: The lexicographic index order is fixed throughout the run.
Every accepted working set has a defined KKT solve or a specified rank-revealing repair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{k+1}\ne W_k\) is selected deterministically even when \(x_{k+1}=x_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but multiplier selection, rank repair, and the claimed behavior of the lexicographic rule are formulation- and algorithm-dependent. An authoritative algorithm statement with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Zero-Step Handling
children.top_down_role: Working-set changes occurring without meaningful primal displacement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Characterization of a Zero Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact characterization of a zero feasible ratio in a feasible active-set iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha_{\max}=\sup\{\alpha\in[0,1]:a_i^{\mathsf T}(x+\alpha p)\ge b_i\ \forall i\}\), where \(x\) is feasible and \(p\) preserves the working equalities. Then \(\alpha_{\max}=0\) if and only if some \(i\notin W\) satisfies \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\) and \(a_i^{\mathsf T}p<0\). Consequently \(x+\alpha_{\max}p=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The admissible step is zero exactly when a tight inactive inequality is immediately violated by every positive move along the proposed direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{\max}=0\iff\exists i\notin W:\ a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i,\ a_i^{\mathsf T}p<0\).

notation.meaning: largest feasible step capped at one

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Characterization of a Zero Step
Zero-Step Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Handles a feasible active-set iteration whose maximal admissible primal step is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequalities \(a_i^Tx\ge b_i\), let \(x_k\) be feasible and let \(p_k\) solve the current equality-constrained QP. Compute \(\alpha_k=\min\{1,\min_{i\notin W_k,\,a_i^Tp_k<0}(a_i^Tx_k-b_i)/(-a_i^Tp_k)\}\). If \(\alpha_k=0\), do not accept an unchanged iterate as progress. Add a selected zero-ratio blocker, or, when \(p_k=0\), remove a working constraint having an inadmissible multiplier. Recompute the KKT system after every status change. Terminate only when \(p_k=0\) and all working multipliers have the required sign; otherwise continue until a positive step or a certified inconsistency is obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero step triggers a working-set change and a new KKT solve; it counts as termination only when the full KKT sign test succeeds.
assumptions_latex: Ties among blockers or leaving constraints are resolved deterministically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k=0\) implies a status update, a KKT certificate, or a declared inconsistency—not a progress iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The step-ratio formula is consistent with the stated inequality orientation, but the multiplier sign test, status update, and inconsistency outcome require a fixed KKT convention and algorithmic reference.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder-proposed example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=0\) and \(p=-1\), feasibility of \(x+\alpha p\ge0\) forces \(\alpha=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed outward direction has no positive feasible step.
assumptions_latex: The iterate is \(x=0\) and the proposed direction is \(p=-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{\max}=0\).
review_flags: deferred_invalid_active_set_example: at x=0 the equality-constrained minimization direction for the stated objective is toward x=1, not p=-1; the example demonstrates elementary feasibility but not a zero step generated by the stated active-set mechanism

children.title: Degenerate-Transition Cycling Risk
children.top_down_role: Repeated or ineffective transitions arising near degenerate faces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cycling of deterministic working-set transition algorithms, distinguished from recurrence of the primal point alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k=(x_k,W_k,\eta_k)\) contain every quantity on which a deterministic transition rule depends. knowledge_statements.title: Nondegenerate Face Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local identification of the optimal polyhedral face under independent active gradients and positive active multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) solve \(\min_x \tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), and define \(I^*=\{i:a_i^Tx^*=b_i\}\). Assume the rows \(A_{I^*}\) are linearly independent, the KKT multiplier satisfies \(\lambda_i^*>0\) for every \(i\in I^*\), and an active-set method generates \(x_k\to x^*\) with constraint-status tests whose primal and dual tolerances converge to zero. Then there exists \(K\) such that \(W_k=I^*\) for all \(k\ge K\). Hence all sufficiently late iterates lie on the optimal face \(F^*=\{x:Ax\ge b,\ A_{I^*}x=b_{I^*}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With independent active gradients, positive active multipliers, convergence, and vanishing status tolerances, the method eventually identifies and retains the optimal face.
assumptions_latex: Primal and dual identification tolerances tend to zero consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ W_k=I^*\) and \(x_k\in F^*\).

notation.meaning: active inequality indices at the solution
optimal face determined by the active constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Convergence and tolerances merely tending to zero do not by themselves ensure finite identification; the tests must be defined and their errors controlled relative to the tolerances, with a retention rule for identified constraints. A precise identification theorem is needed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Exclusion of Inactive Constraints by Slack Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: True generic slack-separation statement, but not a nondegenerate face-identification theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), let \(x^*\in P\), and set \(I^*=\{i:G_ix^*=h_i\}\). If \(x_k\to x^*\), then every \(i\notin I^*\) has a positive limiting slack and is eventually excluded by an activity test of the form \(h_i-G_ix_k\le\tau_k\) with \(\tau_k\to0\). This only yields eventual containment of the threshold-selected set in \(I^*\); it does not imply inclusion or retention of the active indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive inactive slacks eventually exclude inactive constraints under a vanishing threshold, but this does not identify the active face.
assumptions_latex: \tau_k\to0\text{ and the stated threshold test is used}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ W_k\subseteq I^*.

notation.meaning: Inequalities active at the limit point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite active-set identification without a strict-complementarity margin or an error-dominating tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\ge0}\tfrac12x^2\). Its unique KKT point is \((x^*,\lambda^*)=(0,0)\), so the constraint is active but weakly complementary. The feasible estimates \(x_k=k^{-1}\), \(\lambda_k=0\) converge to this KKT pair. If activity is declared by \(x_k\le\tau_k\) and \(\tau_k=k^{-2}\), the constraint is classified inactive for every \(k\). Thus primal-dual convergence without a positive separation margin and a tolerance tied to estimation error does not ensure finite identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a weakly active solution, convergent feasible estimates can remain outside an overly small activity tolerance forever, so convergence alone does not identify the active constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence Alone Does Not Identify Weakly Active Constraints

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ W_k=I^*.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification under strict complementarity and a quantified slack-multiplier estimation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((s^*,\lambda^*)\) be complementary and strictly complementary, let \(I^*=\{i:s_i^*=0\}\), and define \[\delta:=\min\left\{\min_{i\in I^*}\lambda_i^*,\ \min_{i\notin I^*}s_i^*\right\}>0.\] Suppose estimates satisfy \(\max_i\{|\widehat s_{k,i}-s_i^*|,|\widehat\lambda_{k,i}-\lambda_i^*|\}\le e_k\), and classify \[W_k:=\{i:\widehat s_{k,i}\le\tau_k\ \text{and}\ \widehat\lambda_{k,i}\ge\tau_k\}.\] If eventually \(e_k<\tau_k\) and \(e_k+\tau_k<\delta\), then eventually \(W_k=I^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity gives a positive slack-multiplier margin; a threshold above estimation error and below that margin identifies the active set finitely.

Strict-Complementarity Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-set identification from a positive primal-dual separation margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions and strict complementarity: for every index \(i\), exactly one of \(a_i^Tx^*-b_i\) and \(\lambda_i^*\) is positive. Let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*)\), and classify index \(i\) as active when its slack is below a tolerance \(\tau_k\) while its multiplier is nonnegative, where \(\tau_k\downarrow0\) more slowly than the primal-dual estimation error. Then, for all sufficiently large \(k\), the classification equals \(I^*=\{i:a_i^Tx^*=b_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity creates a positive separation margin, so sufficiently accurate primal-dual estimates identify exactly the active constraints.
assumptions_latex: The limiting KKT pair is strictly complementary.
The primal-dual estimates converge to the limiting pair.
The classification tolerance dominates estimation error while tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ W_k=I^*\).

notation.meaning: active set at the limiting KKT point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LICQ Without Strict Complementarity Does Not Ensure Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-activity counterexample separating active-gradient independence from finite identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\ \tfrac12x^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad -x\le0.\] The unique solution is \(x^*=0\). Its active gradient is nonzero, so LICQ holds, but its KKT multiplier is \(\lambda^*=0\). The feasible sequence \(x_k=1/k\) converges to \(x^*\), while \(I(x_k)=\varnothing\) for every finite \(k\) and \(I(x^*)=\{1\}\). Thus convergence and LICQ alone do not imply finite identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique LICQ solution can have a zero active multiplier, allowing feasible iterates to converge from the interior without identifying the constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\to x^*,\qquad I(x_k)\ne I(x^*)\ \forall k.

notation.meaning: Active inequality set at a feasible point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate convex-QP example with one primal solution and multiple compatible multiplier supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\ \tfrac12(x+1)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad -x\le0,\quad -x\le0.\] The unique solution is \(x^*=0\), both inequalities are active, and the KKT multipliers satisfy \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\) and \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\). Hence \((1,0)\), \((0,1)\), and every convex combination are valid multipliers. The primal point and maximal active set are fixed, but multiplier support and a minimal constraint basis are not uniquely determined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicated active inequalities leave the primal solution unchanged but permit different positive-multiplier supports and different minimal working bases.
assumptions_latex: \text{Both displayed inequalities are retained as distinct rows.}

Degenerate Identification Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification boundary when zero multipliers or redundant active constraints destroy active-status separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair for a convex inequality-constrained QP. If some active constraint satisfies \(a_i^Tx^*=b_i\) and \(\lambda_i^*=0\), or if active gradients are linearly dependent, then the primal-dual point need not determine a unique minimal working set. Arbitrarily small perturbations of the data or iterates may classify such an index as active or inactive while converging to the same solution. Therefore convergence \(x_k\to x^*\) alone does not imply finite stabilization of \(W_k\). A valid identification claim must instead specify a selected multiplier, a minimal or maximal active face, a perturbation rule, or a tolerance convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero active multipliers or dependent active gradients can make several working sets compatible with one solution, so iterate convergence alone does not ensure identification.
assumptions_latex: Strict complementarity or active-gradient independence fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to x^*\not\Rightarrow\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ W_k=W_K\).

notation.meaning: working set selected at iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: The Optimal Set Need Not Be a Feasible Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that common-active-face identification can be strictly weaker than optimal-set identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=[-1,1]^2\) and minimize \(f(x_1,x_2)=\tfrac12x_1^2\) over \(P\). The optimal set is \[S=\{(0,t):-1\le t\le1\}.\] It is not a face of \(P\), and because it meets \(\operatorname{int}P\), the minimal face containing it is \(F_S=P\). Thus identifying \(F_S\) reveals no nontrivial boundary activity even though the optimal set is a proper positive-dimensional subset of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat quadratic over a square has an interior line segment of minimizers; the optimal set is not a feasible face, and its common-active face is the entire square.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=\{0\}\times[-1,1]\text{ is not a face of }P,\qquad F_S=P.

notation.meaning: Minimal face of P containing S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common-Active Face of a Nonunique Solution Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical feasible-face target shared by all optimizers of a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a polyhedron and let \(S\subseteq P\) be the nonempty solution set of a convex QP. The minimal feasible face containing all optimizers is \[F_S=\bigcap\{F:F\text{ is a face of }P,\ S\subseteq F\}.\] Equivalently, in a fixed inequality representation, \(F_S\) is determined by the inequalities active at every point of \(S\). Identifying \(F_S\) recovers the common active-face information but need not identify \(S\), a selected optimizer, or the complete active set at each optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonunique optimizers, the common-active target is the smallest feasible face containing them all; it can be coarser than either the optimal set or a selected optimizer's active face.
assumptions_latex: S\ne\varnothing\text{ is the convex-QP solution set}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_S=\bigcap\{F\unlhd P:S\subseteq F\}.

notation.meaning: Minimal feasible face containing all minimizers.

Identification of Nonunique Solution Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes face-level identification when the convex QP has a positive-dimensional optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax\ge b\}\) and let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}(\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx)\) be nonempty and non-singleton. Define the minimal face of \(P\) containing \(S\) by \(F_S=\bigcap\{F:F\text{ is a face of }P,\ S\subseteq F\}\). Face identification means that a method eventually selects constraints whose common equality set in \(P\) is \(F_S\); it does not require convergence to a unique point of \(S\). If different points of \(S\) have different active sets, pointwise active-set stabilization is stronger than, and may be incompatible with, identification of \(F_S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonunique minimizers, identification should target the minimal feasible face containing the solution set, not necessarily one point’s full active set.
assumptions_latex: The convex QP has a nonempty, non-singleton solution set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{face identification targets }F_S\), whereas pointwise active-set identification may depend on the selected \(x^*\in S\).

notation.meaning: minimal face of the feasible polyhedron containing the solution set

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_{x\ge0}\ \tfrac12(x-\theta)^2,\] the unique solution is \(x(\theta)=\max\{\theta,0\}\). The bound is active for \(\theta\le0\) and inactive for \(\theta>0\); at \(\theta=0\) its multiplier is zero. Arbitrarily small parameter changes across zero therefore change the active set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact active-set persistence representation for affine-parametric strictly convex QPs with fixed matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succ0\) and fixed constraint matrices \(A,G\) be given, while \(c(\theta),b(\theta),h(\theta)\) depend affinely on \(\theta\). For a candidate active set \(W\) such that \([A^T\ G_W^T]^T\) has full row rank, the fixed-active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular and its solution \((x_W(\theta),\nu_W(\theta),\lambda_W(\theta))\) is affine in \(\theta\). The set \[\mathcal R_W=\{\theta:Ax_W(\theta)=b(\theta),\ G_{\bar W}x_W(\theta)\le h_{\bar W}(\theta),\ \lambda_W(\theta)\ge0\}\] is polyhedral. On \(\mathcal R_W\), the KKT conditions certify that \(x_W(\theta)\) is the unique optimizer. At relative-interior parameters where inactive slacks and active multipliers are strict, \(W\) persists under sufficiently small parameter changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fixed matrices and affine right-hand-side data, each regular active set defines an affine optimizer on a polyhedral critical region and persists inside strict region interiors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta\in\mathcal R_W\Rightarrow x_W(\theta)\text{ is the unique global optimizer.}

notation.meaning: Critical parameter region associated with working set W.
