Identification in Repeated QP Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local persistence of an active face under small parametric changes in a regular QP sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider QPs parameterized by \(\theta\): \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TH(\theta)x+c(\theta)^Tx\) subject to \(A(	heta)x\ge b(	heta)\). Suppose that at \(\bar\theta\) the solution \(\bar x\) is unique, the active gradients are linearly independent, strict complementarity holds, and the reduced Hessian is positive definite. If the data depend continuously on \(\theta\), then there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar\theta\) in which the local primal-dual solution varies continuously and retains the same active set. Thus the preceding QP's active set is an exact predictor for sufficiently small parameter changes that remain inside \(U\); crossing the neighborhood boundary may change the face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard strong-regularity conditions, sufficiently small data changes preserve the active set, making the previous QP’s face an exact local predictor.
assumptions_latex: The reference solution satisfies active-gradient independence and strict complementarity.
The reduced Hessian at the reference solution is positive definite.
QP data vary continuously with the parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists U\ni\bar\theta\;\forall\theta\in U:\ I(x(\theta))=I(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Convex Finite-Termination Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination for an exact feasible active-set method with deterministic anti-cycling transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a feasible active-set method for \(\min_x \tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), where \(H\succ0\). At each iteration it exactly solves the equality-constrained QP for the current working set, takes the maximal feasible step, and changes the working set whenever the KKT sign test fails. Assume every degenerate tie is resolved by a rule that prevents revisiting a previously encountered zero-progress working-set state. Then the method performs finitely many working-set transitions and terminates at the unique minimizer \(x^*\). The conclusion follows at the algorithmic level only with the stated anti-cycling condition; strict convexity alone does not exclude repeated degenerate working sets.

Equality-constrained subproblems and blocking steps are computed exactly.
The transition rule prevents repeated zero-progress working-set states.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Active-Set Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convergence for convex QPs with flat directions and possibly nonunique minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succeq0\), let the polyhedral feasible set be nonempty, and suppose the QP has a minimizer. Consider a feasible active-set method that produces nonincreasing objective values, solves each working-face subproblem globally, detects feasible recession directions of zero or negative curvature, and uses an anti-cycling rule for zero-progress transitions. If no unboundedness certificate is returned, every accumulation point satisfies the QP KKT conditions and is therefore globally optimal. When the optimal set is non-singleton, the assumptions do not imply convergence to a unique minimizer or stabilization of a unique working set; those conclusions require an additional selection or regularization rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a semidefinite convex QP, safeguarded face minimization yields optimal accumulation points, but flat directions can prevent unique point or working-set convergence.
assumptions_latex: Every working-face subproblem is solved globally with recession detection.
Zero-progress transitions obey an anti-cycling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{acc}(x_k)\Rightarrow \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax\ge b}f(x)\), without necessarily \(x_k\to\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Anti-Cycling Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A state-ordering requirement that prevents repeated degenerate active-set transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an active-set state be the pair \((x_k,W_k)\). An anti-cycling safeguard assigns every admissible zero-progress transition a value in a well-founded strict order and accepts such a transition only when that value decreases; equivalently, it may use a lexicographic perturbation whose induced pivot sequence is strictly ordered. Positive-step transitions retain the usual feasibility and objective tests. Because no infinite strictly descending sequence or repeated ordered state is possible, only finitely many consecutive zero-progress transitions can occur. This safeguard excludes cycling among working sets representing the same primal point, but finite termination of the complete method additionally requires well-posed subproblems and progress away from degenerate states.

children.title: Active-Set Worst-Case Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial face counts and the limits of interpreting finite termination as a polynomial guarantee.

assumptions_latex: A quadratic program in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is described by \(m\) inequalities.
An active-set method changes subsets of constraints and does not revisit a working set under its finite-termination assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite termination based only on nonrepetition permits up to \(\sum_{j=0}^{\min\{m,n\}}\binom{m}{j}\) working sets, which is not a polynomial iteration bound in the joint input dimensions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial limitation of deriving complexity solely from finite face enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linearly independent working set contains at most \(n\) of the \(m\) inequalities. Consequently the number of combinatorially possible working sets is bounded by \[N(m,n)=\sum_{j=0}^{\min\{m,n\}}\binom{m}{j}.\] An argument proving that every iteration visits a new working set therefore yields at best \(N(m,n)\) iterations. For \(m=2n\), the term \(\binom{2n}{n}\) already grows exponentially in \(n\). Thus noncycling and finite termination do not, without an additional progress or structural argument, establish a polynomial worst-case bound in \(m+n\) or in the encoded input length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonrevisiting active-set method may still examine exponentially many constraint subsets, so finite termination alone is not a polynomial-time guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Worst-Case Complexity Boundary

Return \(\mathrm{BLOCKER}\) when the blocker is attained; otherwise form \(r_{j+1}=P_T(Qz_{j+1}+c)\), test its norm before any further division, and set \(p_{j+1}=-r_{j+1}+(r_{j+1}^Tr_{j+1}/r_j^Tr_j)p_j\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Face Minimizer as an Energy Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact characterization of partial minimization for a strictly convex quadratic on a fixed face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(d)=q(0)+g^Td+\tfrac12d^THd\) on a tangent space \(T\), with \(H\) positive definite on \(T\), and let \(S\subseteq T\) be a linear subspace. If \(d_T\) and \(d_S\) minimize \(q\) over \(T\) and \(S\), respectively, then \[d_S=\Pi_S^Hd_T,\qquad q(d_S)-q(d_T)=\tfrac12\|d_S-d_T\|_H^2.\] Thus partial and full face minimization agree exactly when \(d_T\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The partial minimizer is the Hessian-orthogonal projection of the full face step, and the missed decrease is its squared energy distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_S=\Pi_S^Hd_T\quad\text{and}\quad q(d_S)-q(d_T)=\tfrac12\|d_S-d_T\|_H^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from feasible \(z_0\), generate \(p_j\in\ker A_W\) with \(\sigma_j=\nabla f(z_j)^Tp_j\le0\). If \(\sigma_j=0\) and \(\delta_j\ge0\), return \(\mathrm{NO\_DECREASE}\). After a nonblocking positive-curvature update, return \(\mathrm{WORK\_LIMIT}\) only when the prescribed budget is exhausted; otherwise continue.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex QP (linear program) \[\max\ 10x_1-57x_2-9x_3-24x_4\] subject to \[\tfrac12x_1-\tfrac{11}{2}x_2-\tfrac52x_3+9x_4\le0,\quad \tfrac12x_1-\tfrac32x_2-\tfrac12x_3+x_4\le0,\quad x_1\le1,\quad x\ge0.\] Introduce slacks \(x_5,x_6,x_7\), start with \(B_0=(x_5,x_6,x_7)\), choose an entering variable by Dantzig's largest-positive-reduced-cost rule, and break minimum-ratio ties by choosing the eligible basic variable with smallest index. Apply the ordinary reduced-cost stopping test after every pivot. In exact arithmetic the degenerate pivots give \[(x_5,x_6,x_7)\to(x_1,x_6,x_7)\to(x_1,x_2,x_7)\to(x_2,x_3,x_7)\to(x_3,x_4,x_7)\to(x_4,x_5,x_7)\to(x_5,x_6,x_7).\] Each displayed basis is nonterminal, while the basic feasible point and objective remain unchanged, so the deterministic six-basis orbit repeats.

children.title: Numerical Face Misclassification
children.top_down_role: Incorrect activity decisions near tolerances or under poor scaling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and dual activity indicators invariant under positive rescaling of a nonzero inequality row; the normalization does not eliminate general roundoff or conditioning errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonzero inequality row \(G_i x\le h_i\), let \(s_i=h_i-G_ix\), \(\rho_i=s_i/\|G_i\|_2\), and, when \(\lambda_i\ge0\) is available, \(\eta_i=\lambda_i\|G_i\|_2\). Under \((G_i,h_i)\mapsto(\alpha G_i,\alpha h_i)\) with \(\alpha>0\), the compatible multiplier is \(\widetilde\lambda_i=\lambda_i/\alpha\), so \(\widetilde\rho_i=\rho_i\) and \(\widetilde\eta_i=\eta_i\). In contrast, the raw quantities become \(\widetilde s_i=\alpha s_i\) and \(\widetilde\lambda_i=\lambda_i/\alpha\); consequently any fixed positive raw-slack or raw-multiplier threshold can change its classification under an equivalent row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row-normalized slack and multiplier indicators are invariant under positive constraint scaling, whereas fixed thresholds on raw slacks or multipliers can classify an equivalent row differently.
assumptions_latex: The rescaled multiplier is transformed compatibly as \(\widetilde\lambda_i=\lambda_i/\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde\rho_i=\rho_i\), \(\widetilde\eta_i=\eta_i\), while raw-threshold classifications need not be invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Scaling-Invariant Activity Indicators
Numerical Face Misclassification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of absolute activity tolerances under equivalent constraint rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the inequality representation \(g_i(x)=G_i x-h_i\le 0\), with slack \(s_i(x)=-g_i(x)\). An absolute rule declares constraint \(i\) active when \(s_i(x)\le\tau\), where \(\tau>0\). Replacing the inequality by the equivalent constraint \(\alpha g_i(x)\le0\), with \(\alpha>0\), changes its computed slack to \(\widetilde s_i(x)=\alpha s_i(x)\). For every point satisfying \(0<s_i(x)<\infty\), choosing \(\alpha\le\tau/s_i(x)\) makes the rule declare the constraint active, whereas choosing \(\alpha>\tau/s_i(x)\) makes it inactive. Thus absolute slack tests do not define a representation-invariant numerical face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolute slack tolerance can classify the same geometric constraint as active or inactive after harmless positive rescaling.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau>0\) is an absolute, unscaled activity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i(x)\le\tau\) is not invariant under the equivalent replacement \(g_i\mapsto\alpha g_i\).

children.title: Indefinite-QP Active-Set Boundary
children.top_down_role: The boundary between convex-QP guarantees and local methods requiring explicit curvature control.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Inertia-Controlling Methods for General Quadratic Programming

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order boundary for local optimality of a stationary linearly constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point of a QP with affine constraints and symmetric Hessian \(Q\), and define its critical cone by \(C(x^*)=\{d\in T_\Omega(x^*):\nabla q(x^*)^{\mathsf T}d=0\}\). If \(x^*\) is a local minimizer, then \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd\ge0\) for every \(d\in C(x^*)\). If some \(d\in C(x^*)\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd<0\), then \(x^*\) is not a local minimizer. Conversely, if \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in C(x^*)\), then \(x^*\) is a strict local minimizer with local quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT is insufficient for an indefinite QP: curvature must be nonnegative on the critical cone, while strict positivity there certifies a strict local minimum.
assumptions_latex: The constraints are affine and \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\).
\(T_\Omega(x^*)\) is the tangent cone of the polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ local minimum}\Rightarrow Q\succeq0\text{ on }C(x^*);\quad Q\succ0\text{ on }C(x^*)\setminus\{0\}\Rightarrow x^*\text{ strict local minimum}.

notation.meaning: Critical cone of first-order-neutral feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of convex-QP guarantees when reduced curvature is negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the QP \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), let \(W\) be a working set and \(Z\) span the null space of the corresponding active-constraint matrix. Convex active-set optimality guarantees require \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\succeq0\). If some feasible tangent direction \(p=Zd\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}Z^{\mathsf T}QZd<0\), a stationary KKT point on that face need not be a local minimizer. For example, minimizing \(-x^2/2\) over \([-1,1]\) has the interior KKT point \(x=0\), which is a strict local maximum. Curvature detection or negative-curvature steps are therefore necessary beyond this boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative reduced curvature invalidates convex active-set guarantees: a KKT point may be a maximum rather than a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The active constraints define feasible tangent directions \(p\) through their null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\not\succeq0\) permits KKT points that are not local minima.
